nodes.title: Kisin's Hypothesis (1.2.6) (admissible lattice with the Henniart type inside) and its proof for abelian types, Theorem (1.2.8)
nodes.statement: Let p be odd and (k, tau, psi) a p-adic Hodge type (k >= 2, tau: I_Qp -> GL_2 with open kernel, psi a continuous character). Hypothesis (1.2.6) for (k, tau, psi): for every finite E'/E and every 2-dimensional E'-representation V of G_Qp of type (k, tau, psi) there exists an admissible O_E'-lattice Pi with central character psi (a p-adically complete and separated GL_2(Q_p)-representation on an O-module such that every Pi/p^n is admissible of finite length, (1.2.5)) with V(Pi) (x)_{Z_p} Q_p = V, where V(Pi) = lim V(Pi/p^n) is Colmez's functor (Theorem 1.2.4), and a GL_2(Z_p)-equivariant inclusion sigma(k, tau) -> Pi (x)_{Z_p} Q_p. Theorem (1.2.8): if tau is of abelian type (tau has an abelian extension to W_Qp, which is stronger than tau having abelian image) then a Pi as in (1.2.6) exists.
hypotheses: p odd (Section 1.0: 'Throughout p will denote an odd prime').

Abelian type: tau extends to an abelian representation of W_Qp; equivalently (for de Rham V of type tau) V becomes semi-stable over an abelian extension of Q_p, which is condition (2) of Kisin's main theorem.

The existence of Pi with V(Pi) (x) Q_p = V alone is attributed to Kisin's appendix [Ki 6, Thm 0.1] for any 2-dimensional V except p = 3 with residual (omega *; 0 1) (x) chi or Ind omega_2^2 (x) chi (remark 1.2.7); this remark was read but its source was not.

Irreducible V: Pi is the Berger-Breuil / Colmez unitary completion ([BB 1] Section 4, [Co 1] Thm 0.4), and V(Pi) = V follows by comparing [BB 1] Thm 5.2.7 and [Co 1] Thm 0.6 with [Co 2] Prop 4.26 (Colmez's (phi, Gamma)-module paper in its 2007 preprint numbering); none of these was read here.

Reducible V: uses the lattices P-bar(chi_1, chi_2) in continuous parabolic inductions (Lemma 1.2.10), non-triviality of V on non-trivial extensions ([Co 2] Thm 5.1) and constructions of extensions by Breuil-Emerton [BE] Thm 2.2.2 and Breuil [Br 3].
proofSteps: Irreducible V of abelian type (crystabelline up to twist): take Pi from [BB 1] Section 4 and [Co 1] Thm 0.4; the inclusion of sigma(k,tau) is built into the construction from locally algebraic principal series (proof of 1.2.8, not detailed in the source).
Reducible V = extension of V(chi_2) by V(chi_1), with Hodge-Tate weights k-1 of chi_1 and 0 of chi_2: Lemma 1.2.10 gives admissible lattices P-bar(chi_1, chi_2) with V(P-bar(chi_1,chi_2)) = O(chi_1).

Applying V to an extension 0 -> P-bar(chi_1,chi_2) -> Pi -> P-bar(chi_2,chi_1) -> 0 (1.2.9) gives an extension of O(chi_2) by O(chi_1), non-trivial if (1.2.9) is ([Co 2] Thm 5.1); it suffices to build a non-trivial (1.2.9) when chi_1 chi_2^{-1} != chi_cyc (Breuil-Emerton) and a 2-dimensional space of them when chi_1 chi_2^{-1} = chi_cyc (Breuil).
acceptance: For V crystalline irreducible with Hodge-Tate weights (0, k-1) and tau trivial, check that the Pi of (1.2.6) contains Sym^{k-2} (x) (unramified principal series) with the Henniart type sigma(k, 1) as a K-subrepresentation.
Record that Paskunas 2015 Proposition 4.14 (with Colmez VI.6.50 and Emerton 3.3.22) supersedes (1.2.6) for rho-bar with End = k and p >= 5, so R30.6 does not depend on the abelian-type restriction.

nodes.title: Paskunas 2015, Theorem 1.1: Breuil-Mezard cycles when End(rho-bar) = k and p >= 5
nodes.statement: Let p >= 5, L/Q_p finite with ring of integers O, uniformiser varpi and residue field k, and let rho-bar: G_Qp -> GL_2(k) be continuous with End_{G_Qp}(rho-bar) = k, with universal deformation ring R_rho-bar and universal deformation rho^un. A p-adic Hodge type (w, tau, psi) is: w = (a, b) integers with b > a; tau: I_Qp -> GL_2(L) with open kernel; psi: G_Qp -> O^x continuous with psi = det rho-bar (mod varpi) and psi|_{I_Qp} = eps^{a+b} det tau; rho^un_n is of type (w, tau, psi) if it is potentially semi-stable with Hodge-Tate weights w, determinant psi and WD(rho^un_n)|_{I_Qp} = tau. Then (i) there is a reduced, two-dimensional, O-torsion free quotient R^psi_rho-bar(w,tau) (resp. R^{psi,cr}_rho-bar(w,tau)) of R_rho-bar such that n in m-Spec R_rho-bar[1/p] lies in m-Spec R^psi(w,tau)[1/p] (resp. R^{psi,cr}(w,tau)[1/p]) iff rho^un_n is potentially semi-stable (resp. potentially crystalline) of type (w,tau,psi); (ii) for every irreducible smooth k-representation sigma of K = GL_2(Z_p) there is a one-dimensional cycle z(sigma, rho-bar) of R_rho-bar, independent of w and tau, with z_1(R^psi(w,tau)/varpi) = sum_sigma m_sigma(w,tau) z(sigma,rho-bar) and z_1(R^{psi,cr}(w,tau)/varpi) = sum_sigma m^cr_sigma(w,tau) z(sigma,rho-bar), where m_sigma(w,tau) (resp. m^cr_sigma) is the multiplicity of sigma in the semisimplified reduction of a K-stable lattice in sigma(w,tau) = sigma(tau) (x) Sym^{b-a-1} L^2 (x) det^a (resp. sigma^cr(w,tau)), sigma(tau), sigma^cr(tau) being Henniart's types; (iii) z(sigma, rho-bar) is nonzero iff Hom_K(sigma, beta) is nonzero, beta the smooth k-representation of GL_2(Q_p) attached to rho-bar by Colmez (atome automorphe), and then its Hilbert-Samuel multiplicity is 1, except when rho-bar = (omega *; 0 1) (x) chi with * peu ramifie, where it is 2. The source says the result is new only for rho-bar = (omega *; 0 1) (x) chi, the other cases being due to Kisin 2009a.
hypotheses: p >= 5: assumed in Theorem 1.1 and from Section 3 onwards ('From now on we assume that p >= 5 unless it is stated otherwise'); Sections 5 and 7 are explicitly prime-free, and Propositions 6.20 and 6.21 use p > 2.

End_{G_Qp}(rho-bar) = k, i.e. rho-bar absolutely irreducible or a non-split extension of two distinct characters (proof of Lemma 4.6). Split reducible rho-bar and non-split self-extensions (chi *; 0 chi) are NOT covered.

Determinant normalisation of this source: det = psi and psi|_{I_Qp} = eps^{a+b} det tau (p. 2, checked on the page image); local class field theory sends uniformisers to geometric Frobenii and eps corresponds to x|x| (Section 3). Paskunas 2016 and Tung use det = psi*eps instead.
Case split of Section 6: generic = rho-bar irreducible or (chi_1 *; 0 chi_2) with chi_1 chi_2^{-1} not in {omega, 1}; non-generic = (chi omega *; 0 chi), treated as non-split in Theorem 6.24.

Imported, not proved in the source: from Paskunas 2013 [53] the isomorphism E-tilde = R^psi_rho-bar and hypothesis (N2) (Proposition 6.1 cites [53] Prop. 6.3, Cor. 8.7, Thm. 10.72, Cor. 10.71), the block decomposition and irreducible constituents (Lemma 4.8 cites [53] Prop. 5.36 and Cors. 6.8, 8.13-8.15, 9.35-9.37, 10.106, Prop. 10.107), V-check determining non-ordinary Pi (Lemma 4.7 cites [53] Thm. 11.4), locally algebraic vectors of principal series extensions ([53] Lem. 11.5, 12.5, 12.6); Colmez [18] VI.6.50 and Emerton [28] 3.3.22 for locally algebraic vectors in absolutely irreducible Pi(kappa(n)); Dospinescu [20] Thm. 1.4, Prop. 1.3 for (RED) in the supercuspidal case; Breuil-Paskunas [13] Cor. 9.11 (Theorem 5.2); Henniart [35] types; Breuil-Mezard [11] Thm. 5.3.1(i) and Fontaine-Laffaille theory (Proposition 6.23, Theorem 4.15).
proofSteps: Section 2 formalism (Theorem 2.42): for R complete local noetherian with residue field k and N in Mod^pro_K(O) finitely generated over R[[K]], set M(Theta) = Hom_O(Hom^cont_{O[[K]]}(N, Theta^d), O) and Pi(m) = Hom^cont_O(m^0 (x)-hat_R N, L). If (a) N is projective in Mod^pro_K(O), (b) R/ann M(Theta) is equidimensional with all associated primes minimal, (c) there is a dense Sigma in Supp M(Theta) inside m-Spec R[1/p] with dim Hom_K(V, Pi(kappa(n))) = 1 and dim Hom_K(V, Pi(R_n/n^2)) <= d, then R/a is reduced of dimension d and z_{d-1}(R/(varpi, a)) = sum_sigma m_sigma z_{d-1}(M(sigma)). Theorem 2.44 gives (a) and (b) when R is Cohen-Macaulay, N is R-flat and projdim_{O[[P]]} (k (x)-hat N) + max_sigma dim M(sigma) <= dim R.

Section 4: N in C(O) with R^psi -> End(N) satisfying (N0) k (x)-hat N of finite length and finitely generated over O[[K]], (N1) Hom_{SL_2(Q_p)}(1, N^dual) = 0, (N2) V-check(N) = rho^un as R^psi[[G_Qp]]-modules. Lemma 4.3 gives V-check(Pi(m)) = m (x) V-check(N); Proposition 4.9 describes Pi(kappa(n)); Proposition 4.14 shows dim Hom_K(sigma(w,tau), Pi(kappa(n))) <= 1 with equality iff rho^un_n is potentially semi-stable of type (w,tau,psi); Theorem 4.15 builds R^psi(w,tau) = R^psi/sqrt(ann M(Theta)).

Corollary 4.21 (from Theorem 4.19 (RED) and Lemmas 4.18, 4.20) bounds dim Hom_K(V, Pi(R^psi_n/n^2)) <= 2 for almost all n in Supp M(Theta), outside the case rho-bar = (delta-bar omega *; 0 delta-bar), b - a = 1, tau = chi + chi.

Generic case (Section 6.1): N = P-tilde, a projective envelope of pi^dual in C(O). Proposition 6.1 (from [53]) gives (N0)-(N2) and E-tilde = R^psi; Theorem 5.2 gives x in E-tilde with P-tilde/xP-tilde a projective envelope of (soc_K pi)^dual in Mod^pro_{K,zeta}(O), so P-tilde is projective over K (Corollary 5.3); Corollary 6.4 gives M(Theta) Cohen-Macaulay of dimension 2; Theorem 6.6 applies Theorem 2.42 and computes M(sigma) = R/a with R/a = k[[x]] when sigma lies in the multiplicity-free soc_K pi (Remark 6.2).

Non-generic case (Section 6.2, twist to rho-bar = (omega *; 0 1), zeta trivial mod varpi): Colmez's beta with socle Sp and semisimplification Sp + 1 + pi_alpha (Lemma 6.7); Theorem 6.10 identifies the deformation functor of beta^dual in C(O) with that of rho-bar with determinant eps*zeta, R_beta = R^psi = O[[x1,x2,x3]]; with N the universal deformation of beta^dual, Lemma 6.13 gives (N0)-(N2), Propositions 6.20 and 6.21 give max dim M(sigma) <= 1 and projdim beta^dual = 3, so Corollary 6.22 verifies Theorem 2.44; Proposition 6.23 handles w = (a, a+1), tau = chi + chi using Breuil-Mezard's multiplicity computation and Fontaine-Laffaille theory; Theorem 6.24 is the cycle identity for non-split rho-bar.
Theorem 1.1 is the combination of Theorems 6.6 and 6.24 with z(sigma, rho-bar) := z_1(M(sigma)).
acceptance: For each of the three admissible shapes of rho-bar (absolutely irreducible; generic non-split reducible; (omega *; 0 1) (x) chi tres ramifie or peu ramifie) check that the set of sigma with z(sigma, rho-bar) nonzero equals the K-socle constituents listed in Remark 6.2 and Theorem 6.24 (st (x) det^m, plus det^m only in the peu ramifie case).
Check that no application uses this theorem for split rho-bar (Hu-Tan node) or for a non-split self-extension (chi *; 0 chi), whose endomorphism ring is 2-dimensional.
Check the determinant convention (det = psi, psi|_I = eps^{a+b} det tau) against Paskunas 2016 / Tung (det = psi*eps) before combining cycles from different sources.

nodes.title: Hu-Tan 2015, Theorem 1.3: Breuil-Mezard cycles for rho-bar = chi_1 + chi_2 with chi_1 != chi_2, p >= 5
nodes.statement: Fix p >= 5 and E/Q_p sufficiently large (O, varpi, residue field F). Let rho-bar: G_Qp -> GL_2(F) be continuous and isomorphic to chi_1 + chi_2 with chi_1 != chi_2, and R^box(rho-bar) its universal framed deformation ring. A p-adic Hodge type (k, tau, psi) is an integer k >= 2, tau: I_Qp -> GL_2(E) with open kernel, and psi: G_Qp -> O^x continuous with psi|_{I_Qp} = eps^{k-2} det tau; rho: G_Qp -> GL_2(E) is of type (k, tau, psi) if it is potentially semi-stable with Hodge-Tate weights (0, k-1), WD(rho)|_{I_Qp} = tau and det rho = psi eps. Let R^{box,psi}(k,tau,rho-bar) and R^{box,psi}_cr(k,tau,rho-bar) be Kisin's potentially semi-stable and potentially crystalline quotients (Theorem 1.1: p-torsion free, reduced with smooth 4-dimensional components after inverting p). Then there are 4-dimensional cycles Z_{n,m} of R^box(rho-bar), independent of (k, tau, psi), such that Z(R^{box,psi}(k,tau,rho-bar)/varpi) = sum_{n,m} a_{n,m}(k,tau) Z_{n,m} and Z(R^{box,psi}_cr(k,tau,rho-bar)/varpi) = sum_{n,m} a^cr_{n,m}(k,tau) Z_{n,m}, with Z_{n,m} = Z(R^{box,psi}_cr(n+2, (omega-tilde^m)^{+2}, rho-bar)/varpi); here a_{n,m}(k,tau) is the multiplicity of sigma_{n,m} = Sym^n F^2 (x) det^m (0 <= n <= p-1, 0 <= m <= p-2) in the semisimplified reduction of sigma(k,tau) = Sym^{k-2} E^2 (x) sigma(tau). The generic case chi_1 chi_2^{-1} not in {1, omega^{+-1}} is Remark 5.7; the non-generic case rho-bar = 1 + omega (up to twist), the only new case, is Theorems 5.11 and 5.12, which in the versal fixed-determinant ring give Z(R^ver(k,tau,rho-bar)/varpi) = a_{p-3,1} p_1 + a_{0,0} p_2 + a_{p-1,0}(p_2 + p_3) and the analogous crystalline identity, for the three minimal primes p_1, p_2, p_3 of R^ver over J R^ver.
hypotheses: p >= 5 throughout (Notation, p. 1383).
rho-bar = chi_1 + chi_2 with chi_1 != chi_2 (split, non-scalar); scalar rho-bar = chi + chi and non-split self-extensions (chi *; 0 chi) are not covered.
Normalisation (checked on the page image of p. 1384, where the text layer drops eps twice): det rho = psi eps and psi|_{I_Qp} = eps^{k-2} det tau; Hodge-Tate weights (0, k-1).

The proof works with versal deformation rings R^ver(rho-bar) and pseudo-deformation rings R^ps, and transfers to framed rings in Section 6 using formal smoothness of framed over versal rings ([18] = Khare-Wintenberger II, Prop. 2.1).

Imported: Paskunas 2013 [25] (E-tilde = R^{ps,zeta}(r-bar) when (r, lambda) != (p-2, +-1), Cor. 2.12; R^ps = End(N_1) = End(N_2), Section 10; V-check(N_1) universal deformation of rho_1, Cor. 10.72; Lemmas 5.24, 5.27; Cor. 2.5); Paskunas 2015 [26] Cor. 6.5 and Thm. 6.6 (Theorem 4.2); Kisin 2009a [20] 1.5.9, 1.5.11, Section 1.7; Emerton-Paskunas [11] (P-tilde projective over K); Ollivier [24]; Boeckle [2] (Demuskin groups); Khare-Wintenberger II [18] Prop. 3.6 (formal smoothness of R^ver_cr(2,1,rho-bar), used in Theorem 5.12); one global input due to Emerton [9] as stated in the introduction.
Sections 3.1-3.2 (explicit versal rings, Proposition 3.8), 4.2 (Theorem 4.10) and 5.1-5.2 (Propositions 5.3, 5.5, Corollary 5.10) were not read in detail; Theorems 5.11 and 5.12 depend on them.
proofSteps: Section 2: for (H) lambda != 0 and (r, lambda) != (p-1, +-1), the limit pi_infty(r, lambda, chi) of I_chi(Sym^r F^2)/(T - lambda)^n embeds as the subspace of Inj_G pi(r, lambda, chi) generated by its I_1-invariants (Proposition 2.3, Corollaries 2.4, 2.5); the right ideal J = {phi in E-tilde : theta^dual o phi = 0} is a two-sided prime with E-tilde/J = F[[S]] and J = Ann M(sigma) whenever Hom_K(sigma, pi(r,lambda,chi)) != 0 (Proposition 2.9); V-check(pi_infty^dual) = chi mu_{S+lambda}^{-1} (Proposition 2.11); if moreover (r, lambda) != (p-2, +-1), Paskunas 2013's isomorphism E-tilde = R^{ps,zeta}(r-bar) carries theta-tilde to Kisin's theta (Corollary 2.12).

nodes.title: Tung 2021a, Theorem 1.2: Breuil-Mezard cycles for every residual type when p is odd, proved by patching
nodes.statement: Assume p > 2. Let E/Q_p be sufficiently large (O, varpi, k), r-bar: G_Qp -> GL_2(k) any continuous representation, R^box_r-bar its universal framed deformation ring and R^{box,psi}_r-bar the quotient with determinant psi eps. A p-adic Hodge type (lambda, tau, psi) is lambda = (a, b) integers with a > b, tau: I_Qp -> GL_2(E) with open kernel and psi: G_Qp -> O^x continuous with psi|_{I_Qp} = eps^{a+b-1} det tau; r is of type (lambda, tau, psi) if potentially semi-stable with Hodge-Tate weights (a, b), WD(r|_{I_Qp}) = tau and det r = psi eps; R^{box,psi}_r-bar(lambda,tau) and R^{box,psi,cr}_r-bar(lambda,tau) are Kisin's reduced, 4-dimensional (if nonzero), p-torsion free quotients. Then for each irreducible smooth k-representation sigma-bar of K there is a 4-dimensional cycle C_sigma-bar(r-bar) of R^{box,psi}_r-bar, independent of lambda and tau, with Z(R^{box,psi}_r-bar(lambda,tau)/varpi) = sum m_sigma-bar(lambda,tau) C_sigma-bar(r-bar) and Z(R^{box,psi,cr}_r-bar(lambda,tau)/varpi) = sum m^cr_sigma-bar(lambda,tau) C_sigma-bar(r-bar), where m_sigma-bar is the multiplicity of sigma-bar in the semisimplified reduction of sigma(lambda,tau) = Sym^{a-b-1} E^2 (x) det^b (x) sigma(tau). The source says this is new for p = 3 and r-bar a twist of an extension of the trivial character by the mod p cyclotomic character. Corollary 4.6: every irreducible component of R^box_r-bar(sigma)[1/p] is automorphic, i.e. meets the support of the patched module M_infty(sigma).
hypotheses: p > 2 (Theorem 1.2; Section 3 onwards 'From now on we make the assumption p > 2').
Normalisation (page image p. 3): lambda = (a, b) with a > b, psi|_{I_Qp} = eps^{a+b-1} det tau, det r = psi eps.

A.7), the patched module M_infty of [CEG+16] for definite unitary groups with its arithmetic action (AA1)-(AA4), local-global compatibility ([CEG+16] Thm. 4.35, [Pyv18] Thm. 6.1), the faithfulness and density results of Emerton-Paskunas [EP20] (Thms. 5.1, 5.3, 6.3), Wang-Erickson's Cayley-Hamilton finiteness [WE18] Prop. 3.6, the capture family of Paskunas 2016 Prop. 2.7, Allen [All16] Thm. 1.2.7, Barnet-Lamb-Gee-Geraghty [BLGG13] Thm. A.4.1 for ordinary components, and Colmez-Dospinescu-Paskunas [CDP14] Cor. 1.7, Thm. 1.3, Thm. 3.14.

nodes.title: Paskunas 2016, Theorems 2.34 and 2.37: Breuil-Mezard cycles for generic residual types, no restriction on p
nodes.statement: No restriction on p. Let rho-bar: G_Qp -> GL_2(k) be either absolutely irreducible (pi supersingular with V(pi) = rho-bar) or a non-split extension (chi_1 *; 0 chi_2) with chi_1 chi_2^{-1} != 1, omega^{+-1} (pi = (Ind_B^G chi_1 (x) chi_2 omega^{-1})_sm), and let R^psi be the quotient of its universal deformation ring parametrising deformations with determinant psi eps. For a p-adic Hodge type (w, tau, psi) with w = (a, b), b > a, tau: I_Qp -> GL_2(L) with open kernel, psi eps = det rho-bar (mod varpi) and psi|_{I_Qp} = eps^{a+b-1} det tau: (Theorem 2.34) there is a finite set {C_sigma} of 1-dimensional cycles of R^psi/varpi, indexed by the irreducible smooth k-representations sigma of K, with z_1(R^psi(w,tau)/varpi) = sum_sigma m_sigma(w,tau) C_sigma and z_1(R^{psi,cr}(w,tau)/varpi) = sum_sigma m^cr_sigma(w,tau) C_sigma; C_sigma is nonzero iff Hom_K(sigma, pi) != 0, and then its Hilbert-Samuel multiplicity is 1. (Theorem 2.37) For rho-bar = chi_1 + chi_2 with the same generic condition and framed ring R^box, there are 4-dimensional cycles C_{1,sigma}, C_{2,sigma} of R^{psi,box}/varpi with z_4(R^{psi,box}(w,tau)/varpi) = sum m_sigma(w,tau)(C_{1,sigma} + C_{2,sigma}) and the crystalline analogue; C_{1,sigma} != 0 iff Hom_K(sigma, (Ind_B^G chi_1 (x) chi_2 omega^{-1})_sm) != 0, C_{2,sigma} != 0 iff Hom_K(sigma, (Ind_B^G chi_2 (x) chi_1 omega^{-1})_sm) != 0, with multiplicity 1. (Corollary 2.38) If p = 2, psi is unramified and rho-bar is absolutely irreducible or rho-bar^ss = chi_1 + chi_2 with chi_1 != chi_2, then for w = (0,1), tau = 1 + 1 the framed potentially semi-stable and potentially crystalline rings coincide: every semi-stable lift with Hodge-Tate weights (0,1) is crystalline.
hypotheses: Section 2C places no restriction on p, but rho-bar must be absolutely irreducible or have rho-bar^ss = chi_1 + chi_2 with chi_1 chi_2^{-1} != 1, omega^{+-1}; for p = 2 (omega = 1) this excludes exactly the residual representations with scalar semisimplification, i.e. (chi *; 0 chi) and chi + chi.

nodes.statement: Let p = 2 and r-bar: G_Q2 -> GL_2(k) any continuous representation. For a Hodge type lambda, an inertial type tau and a continuous zeta: G_Qp -> O^x with zeta|_{I_Qp} = (Art^{-1}_{Q_p})^{lambda_1 + lambda_2} det tau, let sigma = sigma(lambda,tau) or sigma^cr(lambda,tau) be the locally algebraic type and R^zeta_r-bar(sigma) the local universal lifting ring of type sigma and determinant zeta eps. Then Conjecture 5.1.2 holds: there are non-negative integers mu_a(r-bar), indexed by Serre weights a, with e(R^zeta_r-bar(sigma)/varpi) = sum_a m_a(sigma) mu_a(r-bar) for every locally algebraic type sigma, m_a(sigma) the Jordan-Hoelder multiplicity of sigma_a in the reduction of sigma; and Conjecture 5.1.3 holds: there are 4-dimensional cycles C_a(r-bar) of R^zeta_r-bar, independent of lambda and tau, with Z(R^zeta_r-bar(sigma)/varpi) = sum_a m_a(sigma) C_a(r-bar). nodes.statement: Exact hypotheses of the theorems cited by Dieulefait-Pacetti, as the cited sources state them. (K) Kisin 2009a, main theorem: p > 2, rho: G_{Q,S} -> GL_2(O) continuous with (1) rho|G_Qp potentially semi-stable with distinct Hodge-Tate weights, (2) rho becomes semi-stable over an abelian extension of Q_p, (3) rho-bar odd and rho-bar|Q(zeta_p) absolutely irreducible, (4) rho-bar|G_Qp not ~ (omega chi *; 0 chi); conclusion: rho modular up to twist. Residual modularity is supplied by Khare-Wintenberger/Kisin (Serre's conjecture); the residually modular form is Theorem 2.2.17 (F totally real, p totally split, rho-bar modular). Condition (2) is removable under Hypothesis (1.2.6). (HT) Hu-Tan 2015, p >= 5: Theorem 1.4 (rho: G_Q -> GL_2(O) unramified away from finitely many primes, rho-bar odd with rho-bar|Q(zeta_p) absolutely irreducible, rho|G_Qp potentially semi-stable with distinct Hodge-Tate weights => rho from a modular form up to twist) is deduced from Theorem 6.3 plus Khare-Wintenberger's modularity of rho-bar; Theorem 6.3 is the residually modular form (F totally real with p split, rho-bar odd, rho-bar|G_{F(zeta_p)} absolutely irreducible, rho|G_Fv potentially semi-stable with distinct Hodge-Tate weights for v | p, rho-bar modular => rho from a Hilbert modular form); its local input is Theorem 1.3 with Paskunas 2015. nodes.title: Dieulefait-Pacetti, proofs of Theorems 1.4 and 1.5: which p-adic Langlands results are cited for which primes
nodes.statement: In Dieulefait-Pacetti (arXiv:2108.07577v2), Section 1.2.1, p. 4: Theorem 1.4 (p odd; rho: Gal_Q -> GL_2(Q_p-bar) continuous, odd, ramified at finitely many primes; rho-bar|Gal_{Q(sqrt(p*))} absolutely irreducible; rho|Gal_Qp de Rham with Hodge-Tate weights {0, k-1}, k > 1; rho-bar modular => rho matches a weight k modular form) is justified by Kisin 2009c for k = 2 and Kisin 2009a in general, where 'the second' extra hypothesis of Kisin 2009a (the compatibility of classical and p-adic local Langlands, Kisin's Hypothesis (1.2.6)) is removed by Emerton 2011 Theorem 1.2.1 and Paskunas 2015 Theorem 1.1, and 'the other hypothesis' is removed for p >= 5 by Hu-Tan 2015 Theorem 1.4 and for p = 3 by Tung 2021a (main theorem). Theorem 1.5 (p = 2; rho odd, finitely ramified, de Rham at 2 with Hodge-Tate weights {0, k-1}, k > 1, rho-bar modular with non-solvable image => rho matches a weight k modular form) is justified by Kisin 2009b Theorem 0.1 (k = 2, rho potentially Barsotti-Tate), Paskunas 2016 Theorem 1.1 and Tung 2021b Theorem A. This case division sits in the proofs of Theorems 1.4 and 1.5 in Section 1.2.1, not in the introduction; matched against the sources, 'the other hypothesis' is Kisin's residual condition (4) rho-bar|G_Qp not ~ (omega chi *; 0 chi), and the removal of Kisin's condition (2) goes through Hypothesis (1.2.6).
hypotheses: Dieulefait-Pacetti state residual irreducibility over Q(sqrt(p*)); the cited sources use Q(zeta_p). Their Lemma 1.13 proves the equivalence for odd p and odd rho-bar (irreducibility over F_p-bar coefficients).
Dieulefait-Pacetti's Theorems 1.4 and 1.5 assert matching 'a weight k modular form', while the cited theorems conclude modularity 'up to twist'; the twist bookkeeping is not discussed in the source.

Hu-Tan Theorem 1.4 and Tung 2021a's main theorem, as literally cited, have no residual modularity hypothesis and take it from Khare-Wintenberger; the non-circular statements are Hu-Tan Theorem 6.3 and Tung 2021a Theorem 4.7 (see the hypothesis table node).

Kisin 2009b (2-adic Barsotti-Tate), Kisin 2009c and Emerton 2011 Theorem 1.2.1 are cited but are not decomposed in this packet (Emerton's theorem is decomposed at statement level in the EXT-10 packet for CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility R31.4).
proofSteps: Read the proof of Theorem 1.4 (p. 4): Kisin 2009c for k = 2, Kisin 2009a in general; two extra hypotheses; removal by Eme11 Thm 1.2.1 / Pas15 Thm 1.1 (second) and HT15 Thm 1.4 (p >= 5) / Tun21a main theorem (p = 3) (other).
Read the proof of Theorem 1.5 (p. 4): Kis09b Thm 0.1 for k = 2 and potentially Barsotti-Tate, Pas16 Thm 1.1 and Tun21b Thm A in general.
Match 'the second' extra hypothesis with Kisin 2009a's condition (2) and Hypothesis (1.2.6), and 'the other hypothesis' with Kisin's condition (4) (Kisin p. 2, Hu-Tan p. 1386, Tung 2021a p. 2).
Check where the theorems are used: Theorem 1.4 in Pasos 1-3, 5 and 6 (odd primes, including q, N, 3 and 5), Theorem 1.5 in Paso 4 (steps (1) and (3)) at p = 2.
acceptance: Every use of Theorem 1.4 at p = 3 must be covered by Tung 2021a Theorem 4.7, and every use at p >= 5 by Hu-Tan 2015 Theorem 6.3 (with Paskunas 2015 and Emerton 2011 for the (1.2.6) compatibility).
Every use of Theorem 1.5 must be checked against Paskunas 2016 Theorem 1.1 (residual type at 2 not (chi *; 0 chi)) or Tung 2021b Theorem A (otherwise).
